eli: Heads-up — after merging the kernel-selection RFC updates into canary, we're seeing a consistent ~20-30% latency regression for short-sequence requests when the runtime picks FlashAttention v3. Sample from last night's smoke: seq=64 batch=4 p50 9.8ms -> 13.1ms (flash_v2 -> flash_v3). Anyone else noticing this? :eyes:

maya: I noticed a few failing perf jobs too, will run a focused sweep. Also saw highwater memory ~+200MB on A100 nodes when v3 is used.

sandeep: Can you paste the kernel routing config that led to v3 being selected? Curious if workspace allocator/limits differ.

eli: here's the routing snippet from the canary config we rolled:```json
{"kernel_preference": ["flash_v3","flash_v2","fallback"], "enable_workspace_pool": true, "workspace_pool_limit_mb": 512, "allocator": "cuda_malloc_async"}```

charlie: FWIW, larger batches (batch>=16) saw slight throughput gains with v3 in our perf runs. Looks like win for long-seq / big-batch, regress for short-seq small-batch.

zach: Pasted a quick telemetry query: `SELECT kernel, avg(latency_ms) FROM runtime.latency WHERE model='gpt-2-small' AND seq=64 GROUP BY kernel`. Link to dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/d/123/attn-kernel?orgId=1 (internal). Current table: flash_v2 9.5ms, flash_v3 12.8ms, fallback 18.4ms.

maya: My hypothesis: v3's tiling/blocked attention path sometimes requests a larger temporary workspace which interacts badly with our per-request allocator and the workspace pool. Leads to fragmentation and extra cudaMallocs.

sandeep: Agree. Need allocator histograms. Also check if v3 triggers a different mixed-precision path (bf16 vs fp16) that changes kernel memory footprint.

eli: Quick mitigation proposal: add a policy override for short sequences: prefer flash_v2 when seq <= 128 until we fully root-cause. I'll draft the rollout playbook.

charlie: Also try forcing env toggles to isolate: `FA_FORCE_FP16=1`, `FA_USE_BF16=0`, and `RUNTIME_WORKSPACE_POOL=false` — see if perf flips.

maya: Running matrix now (seq 32/64/128 x batch 1/4/8 x fp16/bf16 x allocator modes). Will post a CSV and flamegraphs by EOD.

sandeep: I'll pull kernel traces from canary nodes and export `runtime.alloc.fragmentation` and `cudaMalloc` counts per-request. If fragmentation spikes correlate with v3, that points to workspace sizing.

eli: Operational plan: 1) add short-seq routing override (canary, then gradual), 2) telemetry: add per-kernel workspace-alloc metrics + perf thresholds, 3) run microbench matrix + allocator traces, 4) follow up RFC if we need an API-level kernel-hint (e.g., kernel_hint: "prefer_stable_short_seq").

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated for kernel-routing override (canary-id: canary-20260318-7).

charlie: Quick note — if we do rollback, make it config-only (no binary change). Keep the v3 path available for later analysis.

eli: Owners: maya (bench matrix + artifacts), sandeep (traces + allocator metrics), charlie (canary watch + rollback playbook). I'll open the shortseq-override PR and link here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maya: Added :white_check_mark: will upload results to the RFC follow-up thread when done.

sandeep: If anyone runs into noisy noisy telemetry, add `?span=alloc_histogram` to queries.

eli: Great — reassigning to the RFC thread for long-term interface decisions after we have data.

charlie: TLDR: v3 looks promising for big workloads but we need a safety valve for small workloads until workspace pattern is understood. :bug:
